title: Study designs and measures of association

steps.tx: Study designs span **case series**, cross sectional surveys, case control studies, cohort studies and randomised trials, each with a defined population, exposure and outcome. Incidence needs follow up over time while prevalence is a snapshot at one point. Association is measured by **relative risk**, odds ratio and attributable fraction, with significance set at p less than zero point zero five.
steps.say: Study designs span case series, cross sectional surveys, case control studies, cohort studies and randomised trials, each with a defined population, exposure and outcome. Incidence needs follow up over time while prevalence is a snapshot. Association is measured by relative risk, odds ratio and attributable fraction, with significance set below zero point zero five.

steps.tx: Case control studies sample by **outcome first** and look back at exposure, yielding odds ratios at thirty percent lower cost than cohorts. Cohort studies sample by **exposure first** and follow forward, yielding relative risk directly. Randomised trials need one hundred to one thousand participants for eighty percent power at effect size zero point five, with **allocation concealment** in ninety-five percent of quality trials.

steps.tx: Exposure to outcome flows forward in cohorts with temporal clarity, while case control flows backward and risks **recall bias** inflating odds ratios by twenty percent. Randomisation balances **confounders** such that ninety-five percent of measured and unmeasured confounders distribute equally. Bias categories are selection bias, information bias and confounding, with differential misclassification raising effect estimates above one point five.

steps.tx: Classic patterns are exposure first in cohorts with incidence in both groups,**outcome first** in case control with exposure odds in cases versus controls, and **random allocation** in trials with comparison of outcomes at twelve months. Cross sectional studies measure exposure and outcome together, so temporality cannot be assumed in one hundred percent of observations.

steps.tx: Sensitivity is true positives over all diseased with ninety percent being good, while specificity is **true negatives** over all healthy with ninety-five percent being excellent. Positive predictive value rises with prevalence from thirty percent at five percent prevalence to ninety percent at fifty percent prevalence. Likelihood ratios above ten rule in disease and below zero point one rule it out, independent of prevalence.

Gold standard is **randomised controlled trial** with intention to treat analysis preserving one hundred percent randomisation benefit. steps.tx: Relative risk formula is incidence in exposed divided by incidence in unexposed, and odds ratio is a times d over b times c. steps.tx: Odds ratio overestimates relative risk by twenty percent when disease is common above ten percent, so case control results need rare disease assumption. Confidence intervals of one point five to two point five exclude null value one and are significant, while zero point eight to one point two include null and are not significant.**Matching** in case control studies removes confounding by age and sex in eighty percent of designs.

steps.tx: Pitfalls include **Berkson bias** in hospital case control inflating odds ratios above two, lead time bias adding three years of apparent survival without true benefit and **immortal time bias** in thirty percent of pharmacoepidemiology studies. Publication bias hides forty percent of negative trials, so funnel plot asymmetry warns of missing studies.
